clue.text: Dramatist's book used in short film

indicators.note: used in says the book's letter is placed within the shortened film
short tells us to cut the final letter from the film genre

parts.note: a western is a type of film

explanation.surface: A playwright's text appears in an abridged movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims WESTERN to WESTER, and 'used in' puts B inside it. John Webster wrote The Duchess of Malfi.
explanation.definitionFit: John Webster was a Jacobean playwright, author of revenge tragedies.

clue.text: Coinage expert giving information to economist

parts.note: word can mean news or information, as in 'send word'
Adam Smith was the famous Scottish economist

explanation.surface: A specialist in currency briefs an economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' looks like money but means the coining of new words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled with language coins new expressions, a different kind of coinage.

clue.text: Exotic dance for one of the Dutch sisters…

explanation.surface: An exotic dance is attributed to a nun from the Low Countries.
explanation.definitionFit: The beguine is a Caribbean ballroom rhythm; also a member of a lay sisterhood founded in the medieval Low Countries.

clue.text: … one with designs on a man's body

definitions.text: one with designs on a man's body

parts.words: one with designs on a man's body
parts.note: having designs on someone usually means desiring them, but here the designs are drawn on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone harbours amorous intentions toward a man.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the previous clue's sister, hinting at seduction, but the designs are inked pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who inks permanent pictures into skin literally puts designs on bodies.

clue.text: Dreadful pain in joint

explanation.surface: Terrible agony in a joint, like arthritis.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the rack is to be in torment; a rack of lamb is a cut of meat.

clue.text: A bit of pride for rugby club left out

parts.note: the British and Irish Lions are a touring rugby side, so a player is a Lion

indicators.note: left gives L, and out says that letter is dropped from the word club

explanation.surface: Part of the pride felt by a rugby club whose winger was dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' removes L from CLUB to give CUB. A pride is a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lions is a pride, so a young member is part of one.

clue.text: O for a note of affection!

definitions.text: O for a note of affection!

parts.words: O for a note of affection!
parts.note: the character O is both a tennis zero and an alphabet character, so it stands for both halves of the phrase

explanation.surface: A sighing wish for a tender written message.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring O (nil) is LOVE, and O is also a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic missive is a note expressing affection.

clue.text: Printer and designer hasn't started flag

indicators.note: hasn't started says the first letter of the name is removed

parts.note: William Morris ran the Kelmscott Press and designed wallpapers and textiles

explanation.surface: A printer-designer has yet to begin making a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' is not a banner but the iris plant; orris is an iris whose root is used in perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a name for the iris, and orris is a kind of iris.

clue.text: Bread man had at lunchtime, perhaps

parts.note: chap is an informal word for a man
one o'clock is a typical time for lunch, and I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone ate bread at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunchtime, perhaps' gives one o'clock, written as I; 'had' and 'perhaps' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An unleavened flat Indian bread.

clue.text: Muscular complaint unknown to mathematicians

parts.note: beef is slang for a grievance
algebra uses x, y and z for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A muscle ailment that mathematicians cannot explain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscular complaint' reads as one phrase, but 'Muscular' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone brawny and powerfully built is called beefy.

clue.text: Just offside here

explanation.surface: Simply out of play at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair or proper; on a horse or car the offside is the right-hand side.

clue.text: Report special deal for leading translator

parts.note: journalists cover a story when they report on it

indicators.note: special suggests the word deal is made into something unusual, reworked

explanation.surface: A journalist reports a special deal for a top translator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges DEAL to DALE. Miles Coverdale produced the first complete printed English Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Coverdale was a pioneering Tudor Bible translator.

clue.text: One way or another, he goes to court

definitions.text: One way or another, he goes to court

parts.words: One way or another, he goes to court
parts.note: a litigant goes to court with a lawsuit, and a wooer courts a woman, both senses fitting

explanation.surface: A man who ends up in court whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooer pays court to someone; a party to a lawsuit attends court.

clue.text: Explanatory list artist put back in magazine

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the magazine

parts.note: a glossy is a magazine on shiny paper

indicators.note: put back says the artist's letters are reversed

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist returned an explanatory list to a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artist' is the usual crossword RA, a Royal Academician; 'put back' and 'in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of terms with their meanings, often at the back of a book.

clue.text: Desperate situation in place in Morocco repeatedly?

explanation.surface: Trouble at some spot in Morocco, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: Morocco is not the country but a goatskin leather used to bind books; binding twice gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma with no good way out; and to bind a book in morocco leather twice.

clue.text: Tribesmen in twice nightly show

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the run of letters
show signals that the words display the answer within them

explanation.surface: Tribal people appear in a performance staged twice a night.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic people of eastern Britain in Roman times.

clue.text: Order to scram is amounting to this?

definitions.text: Order to scram is amounting to this?

indicators.note: order means the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Being told to go away amounts to being shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: being told to scram is exclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion from society or a group, being shunned.

clue.text: Did judge disappear in disorder?

indicators.note: in disorder says the letters of disappear are jumbled

explanation.surface: A judge vanishes in chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessed or valued something, the past tense matching 'did judge'.

clue.text: To deceive maiden is in fashion

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to fashion something is to form it

explanation.surface: Seducing a young woman is trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a maiden is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone wrong information is to mislead them.

clue.text: Way overthrown island prepared for occupation

parts.note: a habit is a way of behaving

indicators.note: overthrown says the island's letters are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A path on a toppled island is ready for settlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' reverses ELBA to ABLE, a nod to Napoleon's fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere fit to live in is ready to be occupied.

clue.text: Medals for British teams in France?

parts.note: onze is French for eleven, a football or cricket side

explanation.surface: Third-place medals for British sides competing in France.
explanation.walkthrough: A team of eleven players is an eleven; the French word is onze.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-place awards are made of a copper-tin alloy.

clue.text: Admiralty official who kept records in code

definitions.text: Admiralty official who kept records in code

parts.words: Admiralty official who kept records in code
parts.note: a naval administrator of the 1660s whose famous diary was written in shorthand

explanation.surface: A navy bureaucrat kept secret logs.
explanation.walkthrough: The diary was written in a shorthand system, read as code.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys was Secretary to the Admiralty and wrote his diary in shorthand.

clue.text: Part of our capital I'm moving into special policy, mostly

indicators.note: moving into places the clue's I'm inside the rearranged letters
special says the remaining letters of policy are rearranged
mostly drops the final letter of policy

parts.note: I'm taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A London district relocates under a special policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly', 'special' and 'moving into' are the indicators; Pimlico is a district of central London, the 'our capital' of a London paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimlico is a residential district of central London.

clue.text: Needlework without 28, note

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the needlework surrounds the letter

parts.note: crochet is needlework done with a hooked needle
the answer to 28 is EAST END, read as the end of the word east

explanation.surface: Needlework done without the East End, plus a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. 28 is read as 'east end', the last letter of EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is a musical note worth one beat, a quarter note.

clue.text: Number of fathoms accomplished beneath sea, reportedly

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece goes below the other
reportedly says we hear the word sea rather than see it

parts.note: sea is said aloud, matching the letter C
able means skilled or accomplished

explanation.surface: A depth measurement achieved under the sea, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives C for 'sea'; 'beneath' puts ABLE under it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A cable is a nautical length, traditionally a hundred fathoms.

clue.text: Story in dispute? No way!

indicators.note: No says the way is taken out

parts.note: a contest is a dispute or struggle
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A story about a quarrel? Absolutely not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like an exclamation, but it removes ST from CONTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A conte is a short story, from the French.

clue.text: He may have major supporting role, or title part in movie

definitions.text: He may have major supporting role

explanation.surface: An actor with a big supporting part, or the title role in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'major' is an army rank: a batman is an officer's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: An officer's personal orderly supports a major; the caped hero headlines a film.

clue.text: It's simple for a boy

explanation.surface: A boy's name is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'simple' is an old word for a medicinal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicinal plant was called a simple; Herb is short for Herbert, a man's name.

clue.text: Inflexible old citizen

explanation.surface: A stubborn elderly resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Byzantine can mean rigidly hierarchical and convoluted; a Byzantine lived in old Byzantium.

clue.text: County I confused with Gloucestershire, in short

indicators.note: confused says the letters are mixed together

parts.note: Glos is the standard abbreviation for Gloucestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: I mixed up one county with Gloucestershire.
explanation.walkthrough: Sligo is a county in north-west Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is an Irish county on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Points out where TV programme is set

parts.note: east is a point of the compass
an end is a point or tip

explanation.surface: Someone indicates the setting of a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders, a long-running BBC soap opera, is set in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC soap EastEnders is set in that part of east London.

clue.text: Whither people retire out of boredom?

indicators.note: out of signals the letters of boredom are taken out of their order

explanation.surface: Where people go to escape tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' here means go to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: People retire to sleep in the room with the bed.
